title: Negeri Sembilan
capsule: Negeri Sembilan ('Nine States') emerged as a distinct polity around 1773 when Raja Melewar arrived from the Minangkabau region of Sumatra, united nine rival chiefdoms, and received recognition from Johor with the title Yamtuan Seri Menanti. Its confederal structure, rooted in Minangkabau adat (customary law) including matrilineal inheritance, distinguished it from other Malay polities; the nine luaks (chieftainships) retained substantial autonomy under the paramount ruler. Succession disputes after Raja Melewar's death in 1795 generated prolonged instability, prompting repeated British interventions beginning at Sungai Ujong in 1874. The modern configuration crystallized in 1895 when the Seri Menanti Confederation expanded to absorb Sungai Ujong and Jelebu, simultaneously entering the British Federated Malay States.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The internal boundaries among the nine luaks are poorly mapped; territorial extent for the pre-1895 confederation is reconstructed from colonial administrative records and is only approximate.
